prompt.summary: Latter-day Saints fleeing antipolygamy prosecution crossed into Chihuahua in 1885 and 1886. They dammed the Piedras Verdes River and laid out Colonia Juarez, named for Benito Juarez, then spread to Dublan, Diaz, Pacheco and other colonies. The first stake in Mexico was organized there in 1895, and the Juarez Stake Academy gave the colonies primary and secondary schooling. Most colonists fled during the 1912 Mexican Revolution; Colonia Juarez survives, and a temple was dedicated there in 1999.
